status: CLARIFIED — two different MC runs produce different D values

analysis_1.method: Targeted Alison circle analysis with 200 MC trials
analysis_1.note: This is the standalone Alison divergence computation

analysis_2.method: 1-degree grid scan of 60 qualifying circles, each with 200 MC trials
analysis_2.note: Rank/percentile computed across all 60 qualifying circles

explanation: Both use 200 MC trials on the same Pleiades data at 50 km. The difference (0.38) is MC sampling variability — different random seeds produce slightly different null distributions, leading to different Z-scores and thus different D.

recommendation.option_A: Use D=8.64 from triplet comparison AND rerun the qualifying circles analysis with the same seed to get a consistent rank. This gives the highest-fidelity D for Alison.
recommendation.option_B: Use D=8.26 from qualifying circles analysis, which provides a self-consistent D+rank+percentile triple. This is the safer choice.
recommendation.preferred: Option B (D=8.26, rank 5/60, 93.2nd percentile) because all three numbers come from the same analysis run.
recommendation.note: Do NOT mix D=8.64 from analysis 1 with rank 5/60 from analysis 2 in the same sentence.
